title: Confinement Versus Screening in the Schwinger Model on AdS$_2$ from Bosonization and Tensor Networks
authors: Sriram Bharadwaj, Jack Isen, Zhong-Bo Kang
abstract: We analyze confinement and screening in single-flavor quantum electrodynamics (QED$_2$) on two-dimensional anti-de Sitter space (AdS$_2$), with and without a Schwarzschild black hole, both in the continuum and on the lattice. The theory is formulated in two frames adapted to distinct choices of a preferred time coordinate: the Schwarzschild frame, associated with the Boulware vacuum, and the global AdS$_2$ frame, associated with the $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$-invariant vacuum. In the massless limit, the static potential between an external charge-anticharge pair is obtained in closed form by bosonization, at both zero and finite temperature. After subtraction of the position-dependent probe self-energies, which, unlike in flat space, are not constant, the potential remains finite as the geodesic separation is taken to infinity, establishing that the theory is screened. This is consistent with the explicit breaking of the $\mathrm{U}(1)$ electric one-form symmetry by the dynamical fermions, and resolves a confining/screening ambiguity in earlier treatments that identify the static potential with the unsubtracted ground-state energy. To validate the continuum analysis, we propose a covariant discretization scheme for placing fermions in curved spacetime on the lattice while ensuring that the continuum properties of the spin and gauge connections are restored in the continuum limit. This construction resolves ambiguities in the existing literature on lattice fermions in curved backgrounds and provides the foundation for our tensor-network simulations. Using a matrix product state ansatz, we confirm our analytical predictions for the phase diagram in AdS$_2$. We perform extensive numerical simulations of the static potential and the electric flux-tube profile for varying fermion masses, which we match to the continuum prediction.
summary: This paper resolves a long-standing ambiguity regarding confinement versus screening in QED$_2$ on $	ext{AdS}_2$. By rigorously subtracting position-dependent self-energies, the authors prove that the theory is screened. They validate this finding using a combination of analytical bosonization and advanced numerical techniques like tensor networks.
main_problem: The primary goal is resolving the ambiguity regarding confinement versus screening in the Schwinger Model (QED$_2$) on curved Anti-de Sitter space ($	ext{AdS}_2$). This required careful handling of self-energy subtractions and lattice discretization.
main_result: The theory is definitively found to be screened, as the static potential remains finite at infinite separation after subtracting position-dependent self-energies. This result is consistent across continuum bosonization, lattice simulations, and real-time evolution studies.
method: The work employs a combination of analytical techniques (bosonization), advanced numerical methods like Tensor Networks (Matrix Product States/DMRG), and time-evolution simulations using the Time-Dependent Variational Principle (TDVP).
model_or_system: The system is single-flavor Quantum Electrodynamics ($	ext{QED}_2$) on $	ext{AdS}_2$, studied in both continuum and lattice formulations, including backgrounds with black holes. The Hamiltonian must be carefully discretized to maintain manifest Hermiticity.
key_observables: Static charge-anticharge potential ($V_{q ar{q}}(d)$), electric flux-tube profile ($\langle E angle$), and real-time evolution of charge/field densities.
important_parameters: Fermion mass ($m$), temperature (zero vs. finite), and the choice of preferred time coordinate (Schwarzschild vs. global $	ext{AdS}_2$ frame).
main_assumptions: The crucial assumption is that the static potential must be calculated after subtracting position-dependent probe self-energies to obtain a physically meaningful, finite result.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the comparison of the screened static potential in both coordinate frames and show the exponential decay of the electric flux profile ($\langle E angle$) on the lattice compared to continuum predictions. Real-time evolution figures demonstrate string breaking.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by first establishing the theoretical framework using two different time coordinates, then deriving the static potential via bosonization (continuum), proposing a covariant lattice discretization, and finally validating these results through tensor network simulations and real-time dynamics.
why_interesting: While primarily condensed matter/high energy theory, the use of Tensor Networks (MPS ansatz) to simulate quantum field theories on curved backgrounds provides a powerful computational methodology relevant to strongly correlated systems studied in AMO physics.

(Left): The regularized static patch coordinates (T, r): in this local frame, the singularity at r = 0 appears as a vertical spatial boundary, and the bifurcate Killing horizon at r = rh is represented as a stationary radial location. (Right): The same spacetime mapped into global AdS2 coordinates (τ, ρ): in this global covering space, the horizon unfolds into intersecting light-like rays (cos τ = sech ρ), and the r = 0 point maps directly to spacelike boundaries at constant global time (τ = ±π/2).

Figure 2: Electric field profile for a neutral pair of external charges q1 = −q2 = q, plotted for several values of the gauge coupling g: global AdS2, E(ρ) (left), and the Schwarzschild frame, E(r) (right). The dashed vertical lines mark the charge insertions at ρ = ρ1,2 (resp. r = r1,2).
